jobs.description:
TekStaff's Client has a current vacancy for a 'Director-Data Retention"

Job Description
The opportunity

We are seeking a senior global delivery leader to establish and lead the program office for the Global Data Retention Management Program. The program will coordinate enterprise efforts to identify, secure, classify and remediate over-retained structured and unstructured data, using a risk-based approach and a common global framework. The role is accountable for turning a complex cross-enterprise mandate into an executable roadmap, strong governance, transparent reporting and measurable outcomes.
This is a hands-on leadership role for a self-starter who creates clarity, builds momentum and takes ownership. The successful candidate will work across business groups and control functions, lead a team of project managers and workstream leads, and engage senior business and technology leaders to resolve issues and maintain alignment.

Key accountabilities

· Own integrated delivery across discovery, planning, execution and transition to sustainable business-as-usual controls.
· Establish and run the program management office, including the integrated roadmap, and master schedule. Coordinate with regional delivery teams on their work breakdown structure, resource plan, financial controls and delivery standards.
· Design and operate program governance, including steering committee, governance committee and working-team forums, with clear decision rights, escalation paths and accountabilities.
· Lead multiple project managers, workstream leads, internal teams and external delivery partners. Set expectations, remove barriers and drive timely decisions.
· Develop executive communication and reporting models covering progress, outcomes, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, financials and capacity.
· Create and maintain stakeholder, governance, communications, change and adoption plans suited to a global, federated delivery model.
· Partner with business groups to sequence work based on risk, readiness, dependencies and capacity while avoiding duplication with related initiatives.
· Drive consistent execution across data inventory, risk tiering, security controls, classification, retention, disposition and sustainment workstreams.
· Ensure delivery evidence, controls and reporting are clear, traceable and suitable for senior management, audit and regulatory review.
· Manage vendors and systems integrators, including scope, deliverables, commercial performance, quality and knowledge transfer.
Measures of success
· A credible global roadmap, governance model and integrated delivery plan are established and actively used.
· Senior leaders have clear, concise and timely visibility into outcomes, trade-offs, risks and decisions.
· Workstreams have accountable owners, realistic plans and disciplined execution rhythms.
· Priority data risks are addressed through a repeatable model that business groups can sustain.

Experience and expertise

Stakeholder leadership

· Operate confidently with Business Group CIOs and senior business leaders at VP and SVP levels.
· Build alignment across Technology, Data, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, Records Management, Audit and business teams.
· Frame complex issues simply, present clear options and secure timely decisions without overloading leaders with detail.
· Influence across organizational boundaries, manage competing priorities and maintain constructive challenge when commitments are at risk.
· Create trusted relationships while preserving clear accountability for outcomes, decisions and follow-through.

Leadership competencies

Ownership and drive
Acts as the accountable leader, anticipates needs and follows issues through to resolution.
Self-directed execution
Creates structure from ambiguity, mobilizes quickly and works effectively with limited direction.
Enterprise perspective
Connects delivery choices to risk reduction, business outcomes and long-term sustainability.
Executive communication
Communicates with precision, adapts to the audience and makes decisions easy to understand.
People leadership
Sets high standards, develops team members and creates a culture of accountability and collaboration. (No direct people management)
Pragmatic judgment
Balances pace, control, cost, capacity and quality to keep a complex program moving.

Why this role matters

The Global Data Retention Management Program addresses a material enterprise need: reducing cyber, privacy and regulatory risk while creating stronger and more sustainable control over data assets (structured and unstructured). This role will shape how the organization mobilizes, governs and executes a complex global transformation, while building a delivery model that can be sustained across business groups.

Critical Skills / Must-Haves:

1. 10+ years of progressive experience leading large, complex enterprise programs, including global or multi-business transformation.
2. Demonstrated success building and running a large program office with multiple project managers, workstreams, delivery partners and senior sponsors.
3. Strong command of program governance, integrated planning, dependency management, RAID management, financial oversight, resource planning and executive reporting.
4. Experience delivering programs in data governance, data management, records and information management, cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory remediation, technology risk or related domains.
5. Ability to translate strategy and risk objectives into practical work packages, milestones, measures and accountable execution.
6. Experience leading federated programs where central standards and governance support execution by business or regional teams.
7. Working knowledge of structured and unstructured data environments, data lifecycle practices, classification, retention and disposition concepts.
8. Experience managing consulting firms, systems integrators and specialist vendors in outcome-based engagements.

Nice-to-Haves:

1. Financial services, insurance or another highly regulated industry.
2. Enterprise data governance, data lifecycle management, information management or data remediation.
3. Cyber risk reduction, privacy, audit, regulatory remediation or control transformation.
4. Operating-model design, organizational change and business adoption.
5. Agile and traditional delivery methods, with sound judgment on where each approach fits.

jobs.description:
Dig Insights unites strategy, human understanding, and technology to help brands move decisively, in a world that won’t wait. We work with insights and marketing professionals at some of the world’s most well-loved brands, powering their brand and innovation decision-making. Dig One is our agile technology platform, used by our people and our clients, to deliver smarter and faster decisions.

Our clients span verticals including CPG, QSR, retail, technology, financial services, and telecommunications. Our work is led by a team of over 250 strategists, insights consultants, developers, and data scientists. We work for a global client base out of offices in Toronto, Chicago, London, and Singapore.

Since we started in 2010, we’ve been focused on setting a new standard for the insights industry – challenging the traditional model and building for what comes next. That means hiring people who are bright, creative, resourceful, and kind. People who succeed at Dig are curious, question established norms and are passionate about helping our clients to move their businesses forward. If you want to join a team that takes themselves just seriously enough to produce great work, we’d love to welcome you.

As we continue to grow, both geographically and in our expertise, we are looking for people who want to join a high-growth and highly collaborative company.

Dig insights is looking for a dedicated and passionate Director, Insights to join our growing Toronto office.

Director, Insights – About this role

Working closely with the Analysts, Managers and VP on their team, the Director provides essential support to their team to help execute and deliver client projects. The Director is responsible for delivering a final report including strategic insights/ research findings, summaries, and recommendations to the VP. The Director has demonstrated their research skills and knowledge and is a key contact for clients on any questions or clarifications. They can be relied on for project updates, recommendations on additional analysis required, working with other Dig team members to develop solutions to any project related problems and troubleshoot any issues that arise. The Director also acts as the day-to-day manager of the Analysts and Managers on the team, providing feedback, establishing goals, and helping to train the team on fundamentals, advance research techniques and report writing. In addition to growing their skill set as a researcher, the Directors at Dig are encouraged to take part in our company’s exciting culture and enjoy this dynamic stage in their career.

Your primary responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

Supporting the sales process through proposal development, including methodology design, costing, scheduling and design considerations.
Overseeing project management in its entirety ensuring timely, quality deliverables according to project design.
Managing a team by guiding data analysis and results communication to ensure projects are delivered with excellence.
Analysing results and creating a "story" that delivers insightful, strategic and actionable answers for clients.
Confidently presenting results to all levels of client organizations in a clear and compelling manner.
Providing advice, guidance and counselling to Research Analysts and Research Managers, including assessment and identification of training needs.
Developing and maintaining client relationships while identifying growth opportunities within existing accounts and consulting/participating in the selling process.

Experience, Skills and Requirements:

7 + years of direct and relevant experience.
University Degree or Post-Graduate Program in a relevant field (Market Research, Business Insights, Marketing, Statistics, or other).
Solid English communication skills, both written and oral are required.
Proficiency in SPSS and/or Q or other tabulations software.
Excellent skills in PowerPoint and Microsoft Office Suite are required.
Able to work within a fast-paced dynamic environment.
Ability to meet tight deadlines, while maintaining close attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and with a team.

Work Perks:

A hybrid-remote work environment, where employees have the flexibility to work remotely or from one of our offices
Unlimited vacation policy
Reimbursement for health and wellness classes/memberships and continuous learning
RRSP / 401K employer matching program
Offices in Toronto and Chicago, located steps to public transportation in the downtown core
Regular social events such as charity poker nights, trivia events, team building days, and more!

To find out more about us visit us at www.diginsights.com & www.upsiide.com

We are committed to creating an inclusive work environment and encourage applications from all qualified candidates including those in the BIPOC and LGBTQ communities, and from people with disabilities.

jobs.title: VP, Finance & Controllership
jobs.description:
Banyan Software is the best permanent home for software businesses that serve specialized industries, their employees, and their customers. With a buy-grow-and-hold-for-life approach and a permanent capital base, Banyan acquires and grows companies worldwide, honoring founder legacies and helping portfolio companies modernize through shared AI expertise and operational discipline. Founded in 2016, Banyan operates more than 120 portfolio companies across North and South America, Europe, and APAC, and has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list for six consecutive years. The Banyan Software Foundation, endowed with $100 million in Banyan stock, leverages technology to build a greener and more equitable world.
The Opportunity This is the operational core of our global Finance function. You will own the close, the consolidation, the audit, and the reporting rhythm that turn a growing portfolio of acquired software companies into a coherent whole.
Banyan acquires vertical software businesses and holds them permanently. We don’t buy to flip. We buy to grow. That permanence shapes how we build Finance: it rewards investment in process, systems, and people that compound over years. You will inherit a function in motion, healthy and growing, and set the trajectory for the next layer of operational maturity across HQ and the operating companies.
You will lead a team across Controllership, Global Payroll, and ERP & Reporting, partner closely with FP&A, Tax, and Treasury at HQ, and work directly with Finance Directors at the operating companies.

Why Banyan A permanent-hold model changes how Finance is built.

Most controllership leaders inherit a function being optimized for a sale or transition. Here, you’re building for the long arc: maturing close, consolidation, and reporting practices that compound with every acquisition we add. The work you do this year is still relevant five years from now.
Real scale, real complexity, real velocity.

Many legal entities globally. A growing collection of vertical software businesses, each with its own data and accounting nuances, rolling up into one coherent group. Acquisitions flow through the close on a regular cadence.
Direct partnership with the CFO.

You’ll operate as a thought partner, not a back-office function. The CFO is looking for someone who can translate the numbers into narrative, surface implications, and bring discipline to how Finance shows up across the group.

What You Own The global close and consolidation cycle.

Own the monthly close across HQ and operating companies under US GAAP. The current close runs about ten days; the working target is five. You will set the path to get there, holding integrity as the floor.
The year-end audit.

Manage the external audit relationship and deliver a cleanly run year-end. Coordinate audit asks across HQ and operating companies. Hold the function to a standard an auditor can lean into.
Group-level technical accounting.

Bring deep US GAAP fluency, particularly around software industry topics. Translate technical positions into practical, operational outcomes. Partner with the CFO on judgment calls that need an executive view. You understand the grey, not just the rule.
Standardization across operating companies.

Partner with OpCo Finance Directors to align chart of accounts, reporting packages, close timelines, and day-to-day accounting practice as we continue to migrate operating companies onto a common ERP environment. Bring coherence without flattening what makes each business work locally.
Controllership, Payroll, ERP & Reporting, and AR / AP leadership.

Lead a team of approximately ten, including a Director of Controllership, a Director of Global Payroll, and a Head of ERP & Reporting. Hire, develop, and stretch the team. Build a culture of delegation, ownership, and accountability so the function scales without you becoming the bottleneck.
HQ Finance partnership.

Work alongside the VP, FP&A on reporting infrastructure; with Tax on compliance cadence; and with Treasury on cash and FX support. Bring connective tissue.
Systems and automation.

NetSuite is the group ERP, with adjacent close-management, AP, and expense tooling in place. Identify and introduce automation, AI, and system enhancements that create efficiency as the portfolio scales.
Acquisition integration.

Integrate newly acquired operating companies into the close and reporting rhythm. Make onboarding repeatable.

 Who You Are An experienced controllership leader.

12+ years of progressive controllership experience, including approximately 5+ years in a senior Controllership role.
Public-company-grade reporting rigor.

You've operated in an environment where audit, internal controls, and disclosure discipline are taken seriously. Whether at a public company, a PE-backed platform with audited GAAP financials, or a leveraged credit reporting to an institutional lender group. Public-company background is welcome.
Multi-entity, multi-currency, multi-jurisdiction consolidation. Required

. You've owned a consolidation across 100+ legal entities, many currencies, and multiple jurisdictions. You know what breaks first when an acquisition lands in the close, and you know how to fix it permanently.
A Big 4 (or comparable firm) foundation. Required.

Big 4, or a strong, reputable firm equivalent.
Software industry experience. Required.

Either in-industry or as a software-focused practice at a public-accounting firm.
Hands-on NetSuite experience. Required.

NetSuite is the group ERP. We need someone who has worked in it directly, not someone planning to learn it on the job.
Strong on technical accounting, with commercial sense.

Deep US GAAP applied to software industry topics. You navigate technical positions and audit requirements fluently, and you balance the technical view with what is practical and operational.
An “altitude” leader.

You move from the close-cycle detail to the implications conversation with the CFO without losing either. You tease out the “so what”: not just what the numbers say, but what they mean and what should change because of them.
A team leader who empowers and trusts.

You hire well, develop people, hold a high bar, and run a team without needing to be in the middle of every detail.
Humble and collaborative.

Ego doesn’t show up in the work. You partner across functions without elbows.
Energized by execution.

You drive things to done. You don’t wait for a perfect playbook before you move. The pace is real, and it’s a reason strong operators thrive here.
Intellectually curious about AI and automation.

You evaluate tools. You bring an early-adopter mindset, even if you haven’t yet led a transformation program. AI is helpful here, not critical.

 Strongly Preferred Private equity-backed, holdco, or serial-acquirer environment.
Track record leading or supporting Finance systems improvements: NetSuite migrations or expansions, close-management tool implementations, AI-enabled tooling.
Acquisition integration experience: volume of integrations matters more than complexity of any single deal.
Experience compressing a close cycle.
Global team experience, including managing or partnering with offshore teams

periodic (~10%)

This is a strategic leadership opportunity reporting to the VP Finance. The Director, FP&A will elevate StarTech.com's financial planning, forecasting, and commercial finance capabilities while transforming FP&A into a proactive, insight-driven business partner across the organization.
As a key member of the Finance leadership team, you will lead enterprise-wide financial planning, executive reporting, pricing and costing analysis, and business performance management. Working closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, Supply Chain, Operations, HR, and Executive Leadership, you will translate complex financial data into actionable business insights that improve decision-making, drive profitable growth, and shape the future of StarTech.com.
This position is ideal for an experienced FP&A leader who enjoys building capabilities, influencing executive strategy, and leading transformation rather than simply maintaining existing processes.

What you will be responsible for:

Lead Enterprise Financial Planning & Forecasting
Own and continuously improve StarTech.com's annual budgeting process and rolling forecasts.
Develop and maintain three-year revenue and P&L plans across countries, product categories, buying centers, and customer segments.
Build scenario models (base, best and worst case) that support executive and board-level decision making.
Improve forecast accuracy while increasing visibility into future business performance.

Deliver Executive Business Insights
Partner with Executive Leadership to provide meaningful financial analysis that influences strategic decisions.
Build executive reporting and dashboards that clearly communicate business performance, trends, risks and opportunities.
Translate complex financial information into concise, actionable recommendations.
Identify and prioritize the business issues with the greatest financial impact.

Drive Commercial Finance & Gross Margin Performance
Partner with Product, Sales and Supply Chain to improve pricing, costing and gross margin performance.
Analyze the financial impact of tariffs, sourcing strategies, pricing decisions and product mix.
Develop commercial finance frameworks that support sustainable profitability.
Support sourcing optimization and inventory planning initiatives.

Build the Future of FP&A
Modernize FP&A processes, reporting and planning capabilities across the organization.
Lead the redesign of enterprise KPIs and performance measurement.
Improve how StarTech measures commercial success and business performance.
Build a proactive, strategic FP&A function that partners closely with business leaders.

Lead and develop the FP&A Team

Establish priorities, organize work and develop team capabilities.
Foster a collaborative, curious and ownership-minded culture within Finance.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of Finance at StarTech.com.

Build a modern FP&A function rather than inherit a mature one.
Partner directly with the Executive Leadership Team on strategic decisions.
Influence pricing, profitability, forecasting, commercial strategy and long-term planning.
Lead high-impact initiatives including:

jobs.title: Director, Restructuring, Montreal | Corporate Finance
jobs.description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

FTI Consulting est un chef de file mondial des sociétés d’experts-conseils pour les organisations qui font face à des crises et à des transformations. Nous travaillons sur les enjeux majeurs de beaucoup de multinationales, cabinets d’avocats, banques et sociétés de financement par capitaux propres, qui sont parmi les plus importants au monde, pour créer un impact qui fait la différence. Qu’il s’agisse de résoudre des questions litigieuses, de naviguer à travers des crises, de gérer des risques et d’optimiser le rendement, nos équipes répondent rapidement aux situations complexes et dynamiques.

Chez FTI Consulting, vous travaillerez aux côtés de leaders qui ont façonné l’histoire, en aidant à régler les plus grands défis qui font les manchettes aujourd’hui. Dès le premier jour, vous ferez partie intégrante d’une équipe focalisée où vous pourrez faire une vraie différence. Vous serez entouré d’une culture ouverte et collaborative qui souscrit à la diversité, à la reconnaissance, au perfectionnement professionnel, et de façon plus importante, à vous.

Êtes-vous prêt à faire votre différence ?

Français

À propos de FTI et du poste

Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI Consulting accompagne les entreprises, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration, fonds de capital-investissement et autres parties prenantes dans la gestion de défis financiers, opérationnels et stratégiques complexes. Nos professionnels travaillent aux côtés des équipes de direction afin de répondre à des enjeux de liquidité, d’améliorer la performance, d’évaluer des solutions stratégiques et d’accompagner les organisations dans des périodes de transformation, de crise ou de changement. Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI offre des services couvrant le redressement et la restructuration, les transactions ainsi que les initiatives de transformation d'entreprise.

FTI Consulting est un cabinet-conseil de premier plan à l’échelle mondiale comptant plus de 8 000 professionnels et des bureaux dans les principaux marchés canadiens. Notre pratique de Montréal poursuit sa croissance et offre une occasion unique de joindre une équipe entrepreneuriale tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de l’expertise et des possibilités de carrière d’un leader mondial du secteur.

Nos équipes de mission sont volontairement de taille restreinte, permettant à chacun d’assumer rapidement des responsabilités importantes, d’interagir directement avec les clients et d’accélérer son développement professionnel dès le premier jour.

À titre de directeur(trice), vous jouerez un rôle clé auprès des entreprises et des parties prenantes confrontées à des situations financières et opérationnelles complexes, en dirigeant des mandats, en développant des relations de confiance avec les clients et en contribuant à la croissance continue de notre pratique.

Gestion des liquidités et préparation de flux de trésorerie prévisionnels sur 13 semaines
Revues indépendantes des opérations de l’entreprise pour des prêteurs et investisseurs
Évaluations de la performance financière et opérationnelle
Mandats de redressement et de restructuration
Procédures en vertu de la Loi sur la faillite et l’insolvabilité (LFI) et de la Loi sur les arrangements avec les créanciers des compagnies (LACC)
Transactions de fusions et acquisitions en contexte de détresse financière et évaluations d’alternatives stratégiques
Mandats de conseil auprès des parties prenantes

Ce poste convient parfaitement aux candidats souhaitant mettre à profit leur expérience en restructuration, en finance corporative, en conseil auprès des parties prenantes et en gestion tout en jouant un rôle concret dans le développement d’une pratique en forte croissance.

Ce que vous ferez

À titre de directeur(trice), vous travaillerez directement avec des équipes de direction, des prêteurs, des investisseurs, des conseillers juridiques et des professionnels chevronnés de FTI sur des mandats auprès d’entreprises canadiennes et internationales évoluant dans divers secteurs d’activité. Responsabilités principales

Superviser l’exécution quotidienne de mandats de restructuration, de redressement d’entreprise et de transactions, incluant des interactions avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres conseillers financiers

Préparer et réviser des projections de flux de trésorerie, des analyses de liquidité et des modèles financiers complexes
Évaluer des plans d’affaires, des initiatives de restructuration, des alternatives stratégiques et d’importants volumes de données liés aux mandats
Réaliser des revues diligentes financières et d’autres analyses en appui à des mandats de restructuration, de refinancement ou de transaction
Développer une compréhension approfondie des activités des débitrices, incluant leur performance opérationnelle et financière, leurs flux de trésorerie et leurs principaux moteurs de création de valeur
Préparer et réviser des rapports, des présentations et d’autres livrables destinés aux équipes de direction, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration et autres parties prenantes
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres parties prenantes dans le cadre de processus de restructuration, de financement ou de transaction
Gérer les équipes de mission et offrir du mentorat, de l’encadrement et des opportunités de développement aux professionnels plus juniors
Contribuer aux initiatives de développement des affaires et à la croissance continue de la pratique de Financement corporatif et restructuration de Montréal
Ce poste nécessite des déplacements chez les clients et dans les bureaux de FTI, selon les besoins

Votre développement chez FTI

Chez FTI Consulting, nous investissons activement dans le développement professionnel et la réussite à long terme de nos employés.

Ce que nous vous offrons

L’opportunité de participer à des mandats de restructuration et de financement d’envergure
Une exposition directe auprès de dirigeants, de membres de conseils d’administration, de prêteurs et d’investisseurs
Une plateforme favorisant votre progression au sein de l’un des principaux cabinets-conseils en restructuration et en financement corporatif au monde
Des occasions de développer des relations clients durables et d’approfondir vos compétences en développement des affaires
Une collaboration avec des professionnels de premier plan en restructuration et en financement corporatif au Canada et à l’international
Des programmes de formation formels et informels axés sur le développement technique, professionnel et du leadership
Une expérience concrète dans une variété d’industries, de situations d’affaires et de types de transactions

Un coach de carrière dédié pour soutenir votre progression et votre développement professionnel

Nous recherchons des candidats possédant de solides aptitudes en comptabilité, en analyse financière et en résolution de problèmes et souhaitant bâtir une carrière à long terme en restructuration et en financement corporatif.

Titre professionnel CPA requis.
7+ années d’expérience pertinente au sein d’un cabinet de services professionnels, notamment en comptabilité publique, consultation, financement corporatif, services transactionnels ou dans un environnement similaire.
Solide compréhension des états financiers, des fonctions corporatives et du fonctionnement des entreprises, incluant une expérience dans l’analyse des flux de trésorerie, des prévisions de liquidités, des projections financières et des plans d’affaires.

Disponibilité pour se déplacer chez les clients et dans les bureaux de FTI.

Expérience préalable en restructuration, en redressement d’entreprise, en financement corporatif et/ou en services transactionnels.
Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale, incluant la rédaction de rapports et la préparation de présentations.
Expérience dans la gestion de priorités multiples et la réalisation d’un travail de grande qualité dans un environnement de services professionnels dynamique et exigeant.
Fort intérêt pour la finance, le conseil et l’accompagnement des clients dans des situations d’affaires complexes.
Capacité et volonté d’apprendre, de s’adapter et de réussir dans un environnement en constante évolution afin de répondre aux besoins des clients.

Pourquoi FTI Consulting?

Travailler directement avec des professionnels chevronnés et des clients dès votre arrivée
Être exposé à certaines des situations les plus complexes et les plus en vue du marché
Développer une combinaison unique d’expérience en comptabilité, finance, conseil et restructuration

Bénéficier du mentorat de professionnels reconnus dans les domaines de la restructuration et de la finance corporative
Faire partie d’une culture entrepreneuriale, collaborative et stimulante soutenue par les ressources d’un cabinet mondial
Construire votre carrière au sein d’un cabinet reconnu mondialement comme un chef de file en financement corporatif, restructuration et services-conseils en redressement
